claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder initially exhibits a BCC solid solution.
The initial BCC solid solution has high lattice distortion.
The ball-milled powder may contain oxygen contamination.
The proposed SPS treatment is 850–950 °C for 10–15 minutes under vacuum or inert atmosphere.
Temperatures above 800 °C activate sufficient Mg and Al interdiffusion.
Keeping the temperature below 1000 °C avoids excessive Mg volatility.
The initial BCC solid solution is metastable.
Sintering at 850–950 °C precipitates a nanoscale, continuous Mg/Al-rich intermetallic network at BCC-matrix grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary intermetallic is likely a B2 or Laves phase.
A high driving force for phase separation promotes Mg/Al-rich intermetallic formation in this multi-principal-element alloy.
Spark plasma sintering provides rapid heating.
Rapid SPS heating promotes nucleation of Mg/Al-rich intermetallics at grain boundaries.
The intermetallic network retards outward Mg diffusion and thereby suppresses Mg volatility.
The intermetallic network retards inward oxygen diffusion and supports formation of a protective oxide layer.
Zener pinning by the precipitates maintains a fine grain size.
Grain refinement and precipitation hardening significantly increase Vickers hardness.
Pore elimination in the proposed temperature window produces greater than 98% theoretical density.
The 850–950 °C material has superior oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to material sintered below 800 °C or above 950 °C.
Samples sintered below 800 °C remain porous, have low hardness, and do not form the barrier network.
Above 980 °C, rapid Mg evaporation depletes the matrix, produces porosity, and eliminates the protective intermetallic network.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome treats temperatures above 950 °C as the Mg-loss comparison regime, whereas the boundary places mechanism failure only above 980 °C. This leaves the 950–980 °C interval inconsistently classified.
